recognize_zh: CD3 染色在表皮下真皮結節中標示出大量膜陽性的小 T 細胞，表皮本身無 T 細胞浸潤（無親表皮性）；皮膚邊緣區淋巴瘤常混有大量反應性 T 細胞，不能因此誤判為 T 細胞淋巴瘤。
features: Numerous small CD3-positive T cells with membranous staining within a superficial dermal nodule
T cells are dispersed throughout the nodule and extend into surrounding dermis
Epidermis essentially free of CD3-positive cells, with no epidermotropism
Small non-reactive (negative) cells interspersed, representing the B-cell component
describe_en: CD3 immunostain of the skin biopsy highlights numerous small T cells within and around the dermal lymphoid nodules beneath an unremarkable epidermis. The positive cells are small and admixed with CD3-negative cells, and there is no epidermotropism. The abundance of reactive T cells is a common feature of primary cutaneous marginal zone lymphoma and should be interpreted together with CD20, light-chain studies and morphology. Findings are consistent with a T-cell-rich B-cell infiltrate compatible with cutaneous marginal zone lymphoma.

ddx.dx: Primary cutaneous CD4-positive small/medium T-cell lymphoproliferative disorder
ddx.vs: This shows a nodule dominated by CD4-positive T cells with PD-1-positive follicular helper cells, rather than a B-cell nodule with monotypic plasma cells.
MF has atypical CD3-positive T cells in the epidermis with Pautrier microabscesses and often loss of CD7, which is not present here.
Reactive infiltrates also contain many T cells but lack B-cell or plasma cell light-chain restriction.
